Pro tips on all grey market notebooks:

Most books are designed to last two years - then they start breaking down after the warranty. Leasebacks, refurbished, insurance write_offs, you never know what you are going to get. The book may have been heavily used. It may have been dropped. It may have never left the original packaging and is in outstanding like new condition.

IBM/ Lenovo = poor quality but most available parts with the lowest prices. You can almost always get any part pretty quick. Often the cheapest to repair.

Japanese books = highest quality, lowest failure rate, most expensive and difficult to obtain parts. Parts sometimes have to found in Japan, and shipped from Japan = quite expensive. Less repairs, but repairs more expensive, like Japanese cars.

Taiwan/Korea/Singapore/ (not Japan, not China) books = usually mid grade or lower quality, difficult to get parts, often lowest book price - shop around. Often spare parts are simply unavailable at any price. Taiwan style book production likes to do batch manufacturing, shipped one way with no returns, discounted for increased failure rates, repairs done here by stripping parts from other broken books. You can get a good book for a cheap price if you deal with experienced people.

With all aftermarket books, you should look for a serious discount on the purchase price - like 1/3 that of a new unit or less. Any more than that you are getting taken. This stuff is the tail end of the industry - it's aftermarket for a reason. A lot of damaged goods repaired, or last years model still in inventory, corporate end of lease books may be very very used. If accident recovery - say a shipping container is in an accident - the entire contents of the container can be auctioned off as a bulk purchase by the insurer - many of the books in the shipment in pristine brand new condition. It is very much a hit and miss affair.
